newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish King invites Clinton to visit Majorca.
newsitem.headline: Spanish King invites Clinton to visit Majorca.

text.p: Spanish King Juan Carlos has invited U.S. President Bill Clinton to visit the Mediterranean island of Majorca to unwind ahead of the July 8-9 NATO summit in Madrid.
U.S. ambassador Richard Gardner said on Monday the King had issued the invitation which Clinton may accept although it is not yet on his agenda.

Majorca is the largest of the Balearic Islands located in the Mediterranean off Spain's eastern coast. Secluded coves and a temperate climate have made it a highly popular tourist destination and playground for the royal and famous.
The Spanish royal family has a palace on Majorca where they spend summer holidays and often host visiting royalty and heads of state.

Clinton is expected to attend the Madrid summit with the 15 other NATO country leaders to decide on an expansion of the alliance likely to include former Warsaw Pact nations Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic in a first wave.
There was also speculation Clinton may visit the ornate Moorish palace of Alhambra in Granada, one of Spain's favourite tourist attractions.
The Clinton visit will coincide with the famed running of the bulls festival in Pamplona which starts July 7 and lasts eight days.
The annual spectacle, romanticised in Amerian writer Ernest Hemingway's novel "The Sun Also Rises", has long drawn American college students, writers and thousands of other tourists.
But Clinton is unlikely to attend the bullfighting festival which could draw the ire of animal rights activists back home.
